title: Free-Floating Terms and Phrases
summary: The complete list (apart from music phrase headings in H 1917.5) of terms and phrases free-floating in constructing phrase headings: [city] Metropolitan Area, [city] Region, [city] Suburban Area (each with geographic qualifier, except for Jerusalem, New York and Washington), and [geographic feature] Region and [river] Region. An extra comma precedes the term when the base heading is inverted or contains a comma. Former free-floating phrases ([person] in fiction, drama, poetry, etc.; [name] in literature; [name] in art; [topic] in literature/art; Estuary, Valley, Watershed) are discontinued. The list is in rules/lists/H0362.json.
validation_rules: Apart from free-floating music phrase headings (H 1917.5), only the following phrase patterns may be constructed on a free-floating basis; any other phrase heading must be individually established: `[name of city] Metropolitan Area ([geographic qualifier])`, `[name of city] Region ([geographic qualifier])`, `[name of city] Suburban Area ([geographic qualifier])`, `[name of geographic feature, as established] Region ([geographic qualifier, if part of the name as established])`, `[name of river, as established] Region ([geographic qualifier, if part of the name as established])`. (H 362 Background, sec. 1)

City-based patterns take the city's geographic qualifier after the phrase, not after the city name: `Atlanta Metropolitan Area (Ga.)`, `Salt Lake City Metropolitan Area (Utah)`, `Dallas Region (Tex.)`, `Atlanta Suburban Area (Ga.)`, `Salt Lake City Suburban Area (Utah)`. (H 362 sec. 1)

Exceptions without a geographic qualifier: `Jerusalem Metropolitan Area`, `New York Metropolitan Area`, `Washington Metropolitan Area`; `Jerusalem Region`, `New York Region`, `Washington Region`; `Jerusalem Suburban Area`, `New York Suburban Area`, `Washington Suburban Area`. Adding a qualifier to these is an error. (H 362 sec. 1)

`Region` added to a geographic feature or river uses the feature/river heading exactly as established in the subject authority file; a geographic qualifier follows `Region` only if it was part of the established name: `Red Sea Region`, `Bull Shoals Lake Region (Ark. and Mo.)`, `Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)`, `Himalaya Mountains Region`, `Bearpaw Mountains Region (Mont.)`, `Tweed River Region (Scotland and England)`. (H 362 sec. 1)

If the base heading is inverted or contains a comma not inside a parenthetical qualifier, place an additional comma between the base heading and the free-floating term: `Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)` (not `Rudolf, Lake Region`). (H 362 sec. 2)
`Estuary`, `Valley` (added to rivers) and `Watershed` (added to rivers and lakes) are no longer free-floating; such headings must be individually established (H 800 sec. 7–9). (H 362 sec. 1 note)

The phrase heading `[personal name] in fiction, drama, poetry, etc.` is discontinued (August 1993); use the free-floating subdivision `--In literature` under names of individual persons and literary authors. (H 362 Background note)

The phrase heading `[name heading (except personal names)] in literature` is discontinued (August 1993); use the free-floating subdivision `--In literature` under names of families, dynasties, royal houses, corporate bodies, countries, cities, etc., and uniform titles of sacred works. (H 362 Background note)

The phrase heading `[name heading (except personal names)] in art` is discontinued (January 1997); use the free-floating subdivision `--In art` under names of individual corporate bodies and under countries, cities, etc. (H 362 Background note)
`[topic] in literature` and `[topic] in art` are not free-floating; each must be individually established. (H 362 Background note)

sections.heading: 1. Formulating headings.
sections.text:
Formulate and assign the following types of phrase headings without submitting proposals to establish them in the subject authority file:

- **[name of city] Metropolitan Area ([geographic qualifier]).** Examples:

  ```
  651 #0 $a Atlanta Metropolitan Area (Ga.)
  651 #0 $a Salt Lake City Metropolitan Area (Utah)
  ```

  (H 790)

  Exception: Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for metropolitan areas: *Jerusalem Metropolitan Area*, *New York Metropolitan Area*, and *Washington Metropolitan Area*.

- **[name of city] Region ([geographic qualifier]).** Example:

  ```
  651 #0 $a Dallas Region (Tex.)
  ```

  (H 790)

  Exception: Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for regions: *Jerusalem Region*, *New York Region*, and *Washington Region*.

- **[name of city] Suburban Area ([geographic qualifier]).** Examples:

  ```
  651 #0 $a Atlanta Suburban Area (Ga.)
  651 #0 $a Salt Lake City Suburban Area (Utah)
  ```

  (H 790)

  Exception: Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for suburban areas: *Jerusalem Suburban Area*, *New York Suburban Area*, and *Washington Suburban Area*.

- **[name of geographic feature, as established in the subject authority file] Region ([geographic qualifier, if part of the name as established]).** Examples:

  ```
  651 #0 $a Red Sea Region.
  651 #0 $a Bull Shoals Lake Region (Ark. and Mo.)
  651 #0 $a Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)
  651 #0 $a Himalaya Mountains Region.
  651 #0 $a Bearpaw Mountains Region (Mont.)
  ```

  (H 760)

- **[name of river, as established in the subject authority file] Region ([geographic qualifier, if part of the name as established]).** Example:

  ```
  651 #0 $a Tweed River Region (Scotland and England)
  ```

  (H 800, H 1145.5)

  Note: The use of *Estuary* and *Valley* as free-floating terms added to names of rivers, and *Watershed* added to names of rivers and lakes, has been discontinued. Headings for estuaries, valleys, and watersheds are now individually established. See H 800, sec. 7-9 for instructions.

sections.heading: 2. Use of commas.
sections.text:
When constructing headings of this type based on headings that are inverted or that include a comma not enclosed within a parenthetical qualifier, place an additional comma between the basic heading and the free-floating term or phrase. Example:

```
651 #0 $a Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)
                    ^ comma added here
```

list.scope: Complete list (except free-floating music phrase headings, H 1917.5) of terms and phrases authorized for use on a free-floating basis in constructing phrase headings (geographic headings, MARC 651)
general_notes: Except for free-floating music phrase headings, the construction of which is explained in H 1917.5, the terms and phrases described in this instruction sheet constitute a complete list of those that have been authorized for use on a free-floating basis in constructing phrase headings.

The phrase heading [personal name] in fiction, drama, poetry, etc. was discontinued in August 1993 and replaced by the free-floating subdivision --In literature used under names of individual persons and literary authors.

The phrase heading [name heading (except personal names)] in literature was discontinued in August 1993 and replaced by the free-floating subdivision --In literature used under names of individual families, dynasties, royal houses, corporate bodies, countries, cities, etc., and uniform titles of sacred works.

The phrase heading [name heading (except personal names)] in art was discontinued in January 1997 and replaced by the free-floating subdivision --In art used under names of individual corporate bodies and under countries, cities, etc.
The phrase headings [topic] in literature and [topic] in art are no longer free-floating and must now be individually established.

Use of commas: When constructing headings of this type based on headings that are inverted or that include a comma not enclosed within a parenthetical qualifier, place an additional comma between the basic heading and the free-floating term or phrase. Example: Rudolf, Lake, Region (Kenya and Ethiopia)

exceptions: Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for metropolitan areas: Jerusalem Metropolitan Area, New York Metropolitan Area, and Washington Metropolitan Area.
Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for regions: Jerusalem Region, New York Region, and Washington Region.
Add no geographic qualifier to the following headings for suburban areas: Jerusalem Suburban Area, New York Suburban Area, and Washington Suburban Area.
